speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Joan has the bread on. If thou art going to be useful, be useful before the children find thee.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am considering Tuesday. That is a kind of use.

speaker: joan_shakespeare
text: Tuesday is twelve men and a frame, brother, and thou art not one of the twelve until seven of the clock. The children are mine till then. I will not have them delivered back with a play in them.

speaker: mary_shakespeare
text: You're thin, son. Sit, and take the heel. A man who lifts oak on an empty stomach is showing off, and then he sits down.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Mother.

speaker: mary_shakespeare
text: I have said it. The twenty shillings is already gone into Sadler's oak. Do not tell it again as if it were still in the belt.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: She is right. Thou saidst it at the bakehouse, and the children heard, and Judith will have spent it in a story by dinner. It is spent. Twenty shillings. Thursday.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I know where it went. I am not offering it twice.

speaker: joan_shakespeare
text: Then know the rest. I want the hall clear by six tomorrow. Poles in a yard are not my affair. Porridge is. Edmund will try to come, and he is for school.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Edmund stays. I'll tell him.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Thou wilt tell him, and he will come as far as the lane, and Richard will send him back. Let Richard say it. Richard is believed.

speaker: mary_shakespeare
text: Put the dry pease above the wet, when thou art done considering. The sack split. It is a rule that asks no learning.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I'll shift the sack.

speaker: joan_shakespeare
text: And the cuff. Thou hast ink on it from Saturday. Let me have the brush before Mother makes a sermon of a sleeve.

speaker: mary_shakespeare
text: I have seen the sleeve. That is enough for a working day. The grey at thy temple I have also seen, and I am not discussing it.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Good. Then the matter left is seven of the clock, twelve men, and thou home when the ale starts. The cousin pays the ale. Thou dost not stay to be thanked.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will not stay.

speaker: joan_shakespeare
text: He will stay if a carpenter tells him he lifts well. I have met my brother.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will not stay, Joan. Twelve men, and I am one pair of hands, and then I am home.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Say it in the yard, where the poles are, and not to us. We have heard promises that fit a kitchen. Twelve is a number a kitchen cannot spend.

speaker: joan_shakespeare
text: Six of the clock is porridge, not a speech. I want the hall clear, and I want the orchard sheet left on its bench.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The hall will be clear. I am not taking the sheet to a barn.

speaker: mary_shakespeare
text: Eat the heel, son. The frame will still be there if thou art late by a creed. It will not be there if thou art clever at it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Seven. I'll be the dull one.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Dull is a promise I can spend. Clever is a promise I have already had.
